graphEditor.helpBodyOps:
Basic operations

Create a node

  1. Browse node types in the left node palette
  2. Left-drag a type
  3. Drop on the center canvas
  4. The node appears with its color and ports

Connect nodes

  1. Left-drag from a node’s right output port
  2. Drop on another node’s left input port
  3. A gray Bézier edge is created (matches source color)

Select & edit

  • Click node — select (dashed border); right panel shows config
  • Click empty — clear selection
  • When selected — edit parameters in the property panel
  • Label — change display name in the name field

Delete

  • Select → Delete — removes node and connected edges

Canvas

  • Left-drag — move node (40px grid snap)
  • Middle-drag — pan
  • Wheel — zoom
graphEditor.helpBodyFile:
File operations

New (Ctrl + N)

Clear canvas and property panel for a new graph.

Open (Ctrl + O)

Load a saved .json graph; canvas restores fully.

Save (Ctrl + S)

Write the full editor state to .json.

  • Includes nodes, edges, positions
  • UTF-8 encoding

Save As (Ctrl + Shift + S)

Save to a new .json path.

JSON shape

Top-level fields:

  • schema_version
  • name / description
  • nodes — id / type / op / label / config / position
  • edges — from_node / from_port / to_node / to_port
  • layout — legacy layout info
  • external_variables
graphEditor.helpBodyPreview:
Live preview

The property panel shows a Preview Value for the selected node while you edit.

How it works

  1. Select a node → compile whole graph → evaluate with the DAG engine
  2. Show the selected node’s value

Auto-refresh when

  • Selection changes
  • Config changes (value / path / operator)
  • Nodes or edges are added/removed

Formats

  • Number — 6 decimal places
  • Uncomputable — “(cannot compute)” (usually incomplete inputs)
  • Error — “Error: …”
  • None selected — “—”

graphEditor.helpBodyNodeConfig:
Node configuration

Property panel

  • Shows all configurable fields for the selected node
  • Name — display label (CJK OK)
  • Type — read-only
  • Operation — unary/binary op type
  • Value — const node output
  • Var path — variable reference path
  • Default / min / max / step — user_input ranges
graphEditor.helpBodyCompilation:
Compilation

Editor graph → DAG

  1. Collect — collect_document() gathers nodes/edges
  2. Compile — compile_graph() to DAG engine format
  3. Evaluate — evaluate_graph() runs the DAG

Auto output detection

No manual Section config: the compiler scans output nodes:

  • Find type="output" nodes
  • Walk upstream to the real compute node
  • Use the output node’s label as the output name

Composite nodes

type="composite" recursively compiles the inner subgraph:

  • Produces a DAGSubgraph
  • Bindings from subgraph user_input
  • Outputs from subgraph output nodes
graphEditor.helpBodyJsonFormat:
JSON format

Document

{
  "schema_version": "calc-graph-v1",
  "name": "graph name",
  "description": "graph description",
  "nodes": [...],
  "edges": [...],
  "layout": {"sections": [...]},
  "external_variables": {}
}

Node object

{
  "id": "unique id",
  "type": "const|var|user_input|unary|binary|condition|output|composite",
  "op": "op string",
  "label": "display name",
  "config": { "value": 0.0, "path": "", "default": 0, ... },
  "position": {"x": 0, "y": 0}
}

Composite extras

  • config.source_graph — embedded subgraph JSON string
  • config.package_name — source package name
graphEditor.helpBodyOverview:
Formula Graph Editor

A visual node editor for building math pipelines by drag-and-drop,

then exporting JSON for other tools.

Concepts

  • Node — unit of computation (const, var, ops, …)
  • Wire — data edge from output to input
  • Graph — nodes + wires forming a pipeline
  • Composite — a whole subgraph packed as one node

Workflow

  1. Drag nodes from the left palette onto the canvas
  2. Wire output ports to input ports
  3. Select a node; configure it in the right panel
  4. Mark finals with output nodes
  5. Save .json or use live preview

Use cases

  • Game formula design & debug
  • Multi-step math visualization
  • Documenting / sharing calc logic
  • Batch eval with the DAG engine
graphEditor.helpBodyInterface:
UI layout

Classic three-pane layout:

Left: NodePanel

All node types by category. Drag onto the canvas to create.

  • Basic — const, unary, binary, condition
  • Input — var, user_input
  • Output — output markers
  • Packages — imported composites (purple)

Center: Canvas

  • Drag nodes (grid snap)
  • Drag wires from ports (gray Bézier)
  • Click to select (dashed border)
  • Delete removes node + edges
  • Middle-drag pans; wheel zooms

Right: PropPanel

Edit the selected node; live preview at the bottom.
graphEditor.helpBodyNodes:
Node types

Each type has different behavior and config options.
graphEditor.helpBodyNodeConst:
Const node

Fixed numeric output.

Config

  • Value — float (±1e9, 4 decimals)

Uses

  • Binary baselines (+1, ×2, …)
  • Fixed coefficients
  • Condition compare baselines
graphEditor.helpBodyNodeVar:
Var node

Reads a value from DataContext by path at runtime.

Config

  • Path — e.g. character.基础攻击, weapon.攻击力+

Path format

Dotted: source.field

  • character.xxx
  • weapon.xxx
  • equipment.xxx
  • enemy.xxx
  • computed.xxx

Note

Paths should be declared in external_variables; otherwise compile fills defaults.
graphEditor.helpBodyNodeUserInput:
User input node

Runtime user value; ComputeSheet turns it into an editable control.

Config

  • Default
  • Min
  • Max
  • Step

Control inference

  • float/int + min/max → slider + spinbox
  • bool → toggle/checkbox
  • str → combo
graphEditor.helpBodyNodeUnary:
Unary node

One input → math op → output.

Input

  • Value — from upstream

Ops

OpMeaningExample (in=4)
negNegate-4
floorFloor4
ceilCeil4
absAbsolute4
sqrtSquare root2
lnNatural log~1.386
log10Log base 10~0.602
sinSine (radians)~-0.757
cosCosine (radians)~-0.653
tanTangent (radians)~1.158

Notes

  • sqrt — input ≥ 0
  • ln / log10 — input > 0
  • Trig uses radians (convert deg × π / 180)
graphEditor.helpBodyNodeBinary:
Binary node

Two inputs, eight ops.

Inputs

  • Left
  • Right

Ops

OpMeaningExample
+Add3 + 5 = 8
-Sub10 - 3 = 7
*Mul4 × 3 = 12
/Div (float)10 / 3 = 3.3333
^Pow2 ^ 3 = 8
modModulo7 mod 3 = 1
minMinimummin(3, 7) = 3
maxMaximummax(3, 7) = 7

Notes

  • / is always float division
  • ^ supports real exponents (4 ^ 0.5 = 2)
graphEditor.helpBodyNodeCondition:
Condition node

Pick one of two values — like cond ? then : else.

Inputs

  • Port 0 (cond) — 0 false, nonzero true
  • Port 1 (then)
  • Port 2 (else)

Behavior

Outputs else when cond is 0, otherwise then.
graphEditor.helpBodyNodeOutput:
Output marker

Marks an important result; the compiler collects all output nodes as named outputs.

Traits

  • No computation — marker only
  • Compile walks to the upstream source
  • Every output node becomes a named output

Usage

Wire an output node to the end of a chain — no extra config.
graphEditor.helpBodyNodeComposite:
Composite node

Pack a whole subgraph into one node (import JSON/ZIP).

Traits

  • Ports inferred from subgraph user_input / output
  • Double-click opens the subgraph editor
  • Can be shipped as ZIP

Import

  • Open the left Packages tab
  • Click + Import package
  • Pick .json (one) or .zip (many)

endfield.helpBodyOverview:
Endfield Damage Calculator

A PySide6 damage-calc helper for Arknights: Endfield.
Pick a character and weapon, inspect attributes and damage zones, and optimize loadouts.

Basic flow

  1. Pick character — choose from the dropdown
  2. Pick weapon — list is filtered by character weapon type
  3. Set params — level, pot, trust, skill levels, …
  4. Confirm — click Confirm Selection
  5. Read results — character / weapon columns + zone chain + total damage refresh

Window layout

Two tabs: Calc (default) and Advanced.

  • Changing character or weapon recalculates automatically
  • After editing level/trust/skills the button shows “Pending update” — confirm again
endfield.helpBodyMainLayout:
Calc tab — five columns

The main UI is five columns:

Col 1: Character

Pick the character and related params:

  • Character — dropdown
  • Rarity
  • Level — affects stats
  • Potential — 0–6
  • Trust — percent
  • Skill level — active skill

Col 2: Weapon

Weapons filtered by character type:

  • Weapon — dropdown
  • Rarity
  • Level
  • Weapon skills — normal skill level + special toggle

Col 3: Character stats

After confirm, final character panel:

  • Base stats (ATK, DEF, HP, …)
  • Abilities (STR / AGI / INT / WIL)
  • Advanced (crit rate / crit damage, …)

Col 4: Weapon stats

After confirm:

  • Base ATK
  • Bonus attributes
  • Special ability notes

Col 5: Damage zones

All 15 damage zones after confirm:

  • Ability bonuses
  • ATK bonuses
  • Defense mitigation
  • Damage bonuses
  • Crit / crit damage
  • Final damage
endfield.helpBodyMainOps:
Calc tab — workflow

  1. Pick character in the character dropdown.
  2. Pick weapon — list is filtered to compatible types.
  3. Set params — level, pot, trust, skill levels, …
  4. Click Confirm Selection:
    • Button is at the bottom of column 5
    • The same confirm exists on the Advanced tab
    • Refreshes character/weapon columns, zones, and total damage
  5. Read results in each column.

Tip: after editing level/trust/skills the confirm button turns orange (“Pending update”) — click again to refresh.
endfield.helpBodyCharParams:
Character parameters

Rarity

Star rarity; affects growth curves.

Level

Character level (1–90). Base stats follow the growth curve.

Potential

Potential 0–6 (duplicates). May grant flat bonuses or other effects.

Trust

Trust 0–200%; raised via combat/use; affects some stats.

Skill level

Active skill level (1–12). Higher level → higher multipliers.
endfield.helpBodyWeaponParams:
Weapon parameters

Weapon type

Types (sword, gun, staff, …); characters only equip matching types.

Rarity & level

Affect base ATK.

Normal skill

Built-in skill (Lv.1–10) with fixed stat bonuses.

Special skill

Some weapons have specials that need conditions; toggle Enable to turn on.
endfield.helpBodyAdvancedOverview:
Advanced tab — three columns

Open via “Go to Advanced” or the top tabs for extra settings.

Left — Actions

  • Back to Calc
  • Confirm Selection — same as Calc tab
  • Data sources & license
  • Donate
  • Help — this document
  • Search history

Center — Search

Full equipment search:

  • Parallel workers
  • Fixed gear (0–4 pieces)
  • Start full search

Right — Multi-skill counts

  • Enable “Use manual counts” for per-segment counts
  • Combat / combo / ultimate (etc.) hit counts
  • Extra bonus tweaks
endfield.helpBodyFullSearch:
Full search

Enumerates all equipment combinations and finds the highest-damage loadouts.

Steps

  1. Set character, weapon, and other params on Advanced
  2. Configure search:
    • Workers — CPU threads (≤ core count recommended)
    • Fixed gear — lock 0–4 pieces to shrink the space
  3. Click Start Search
  4. Wait (depends on pool size and hardware)

ETA

An estimate is shown first. If too long:

  • Lock more fixed gear
  • Narrow equipment kinds
  • Use quick preview instead of full search
endfield.helpBodyMultiSkill:
Multi-skill & manual counts

Use manual counts

When checked, set how often each skill segment fires:

  • Combat skill
  • Combo
  • Ultimate
  • Abnormals

Damage scope

  • Skills only
  • Abnormals only
  • Skills + abnormals (default)

Expected damage

When checked, averages by crit rate instead of a single hit — better for long fights.
endfield.helpBodySearchModes:
Search modes

Several modes for different needs:

Single-hit damage

One segment of the current skill — quick skill check.

Zone snapshot

All 15 zones in detail — understand the damage stack.

Single-skill preview

Fast preview across gear samples — much quicker than full search.

Multi-skill preview

With manual counts on, preview weighted total damage.

Full search (Top-N)

All combinations; returns top N loadouts (default N=20).

MVP resume

Refine top full-search results with a finer pass.
endfield.helpBodyFeatures:
Extra features

OCR loadout from screenshots

  1. Click Screenshot OCR on the bottom bar
  2. Pick a folder of character-panel screenshots
  3. The tool fills character / gear fields

First run: download OCR models via the dialog button.

Damage dashboard

After confirm: Tools & Share → Damage Dashboard

  • Rotation pie — share per skill segment
  • Zone bars — contribution of each zone

Multi-preset compare

  1. Import/export presets: Tools & Share → Import / Export Preset
  2. Compare: Tools & Share → Compare Presets

Enemy params

On Advanced, tune the target:

  • Defense
  • Elemental resist
  • Ignore resist
  • Imbalance vulnerability
  • Imbalance state toggle
endfield.helpBodyNga:
NGA Endfield mechanics checklist

Implements the community 15-zone model, physical/arts abnormals, imbalance, execute, heal, etc. Repo doc: docs/nga-46094556-终末地机制对照与待办.md

Abnormal ranks (L0–L4)

Advanced matrix columns L0–L4 map to calc ranks 1–5 (stacks consumed). Key format 猛击:2 means L2.

Forced arts abnormal

Prefix 强制: (e.g. 强制:电磁异常:0) for no initial abnormal damage (G11).

True damage

Enemy panel “True damage” forces the defense zone to 1.0.

Break DEF vs physical abnormal

“Break DEF stacks” is a separate debuff vulnerability, unrelated to 碎甲/猛击 in the matrix. Consuming attacks reduce stacks (see physical_abnormal_state.py).

Consumables / break / SP

“Extra bonus tweaks” can apply NGA consumable presets; execute/heal dialogs include SP, ultimate charge, burn intake, and imbalance buildup estimates.

Execute / heal

Advanced “Execute/Heal estimate” uses current loadout and enemy tier.
endfield.helpBodyTips:
Tips & FAQ

Shortcuts

  • Switch character — dropdown; weapons refilter automatically
  • Tooltips — hover controls for hints
  • Zones — expand/collapse each zone for detail

FAQ

Q: Params changed but numbers didn’t?
A: Click Confirm Selection (or Pending update).

Q: How long is full search?
A: Depends on pool size and fixed gear — seconds to minutes. Check the ETA first.

Q: Where does data come from?
A: Public wiki + community. See Data sources & license.

Q: Matches in-game exactly?
A: Reference only; feedback welcome if it drifts.

Q: How to report bugs / ideas?
A: Open a GitHub Issue (bug or feature).

designer.helpBodyOverview:
Data Designer

A graphical tool for maintaining character, weapon, and equipment data.
Formula inversion, editing, and browsing — no coding required.

Launch

python main_designer.py

Tabs

  1. Formula Inversion — infer growth formula parameters from level stats
  2. Data Editor — add / edit / delete characters, weapons, equipment
  3. Data Browser — browse character / weapon / equipment lists
designer.helpBodyInverse:
Formula Inversion

Infer growth-formula parameters from known level values. Useful when you:

  • Know Lv.1 and Lv.90 stats and want the curve in between
  • Want to verify entered data against the game formula
  • Compare growth across rarities / types

Steps

  1. Pick a data kind (e.g. attributes Lv.90 or skill Lv.9–12)
  2. Paste the numeric series into the input box
  3. Click Calculate / Invert
  4. Review fitted parameters and the curve

Supported kinds

  • Attributes Lv.90 — per-attribute values at level 90
  • Skill Lv.9–12 — skill multipliers across levels
  • Other custom series
designer.helpBodyDataEdit:
Data Editor

CRUD UI for characters, weapons, and equipment.

Sub-tabs

Characters

  • View and edit character stats
  • Name, type, rarity, abilities, …
  • Edit skill JSON
  • Saving refreshes the cache

Weapons

  • View and edit weapon stats
  • Base ATK, bonuses, specials, …
  • Weapon skill data
  • Saving refreshes the cache

Equipment

  • View and edit equipment
  • Affixes, set effects, …
  • Saving refreshes the cache

How to use

  • Select a row; the detail panel shows the entry
  • Click Save when done
  • The calculator picks up the latest data after save
designer.helpBodyDataBrowse:
Data Browser

List view of characters, weapons, and equipment for quick checks.

Steps

  1. Pick a data kind in the top combo (character / weapon / equipment)
  2. Browse the list
  3. Click an entry for details on the side or bottom

Features

  • List mode for fast scanning
  • Detail mode for full structure
  • Search / filter by name or keyword
  • Pretty-printed JSON preview
designer.helpBodyTools:
Bottom Bar

BWIKI Sync

The green BWIKI Sync button pulls the latest Endfield wiki data:

  • Characters
  • Weapons
  • Equipment
  • Auto-saves locally when done

Handy after game version updates.

Data Entry

The Data Entry tab provides form-based creation:

  • Characters — name, type, rarity, abilities, base ATK, skill JSON
  • Weapons — name, type, rarity, base ATK, bonuses, specials
designer.helpBodyTips:
Tips & FAQ

Tips

  • Always click Save after edits
  • Try multiple inversion inputs and compare results
  • Use filters in the browser to find entries quickly
  • After adding characters/weapons, refresh the calculator to see them

FAQ

Q: Calculator unchanged after edits?
A: Designer and calculator share the same data files. Restart the calculator or click Confirm Selection.

Q: How do I back up data?
A: Copy files under games/endfield/data/.

Q: Bulk add characters/weapons?
A: Use the Data Entry tab one-by-one, or scripts for batch work.
